newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks trade mixed amid selling pressure.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks trade mixed amid selling pressure.

text.p: Zimbabwean stocks ended the week mixed on Friday as profit-taking hit second tier stocks, dealers said.
"The market seems to be coming down under selling pressure. Second tier stocks seem to be the ones mainly affected while quality blue-chip counters are holding their own," one broker said.
The main 57-share industrial index eased 3.71 points to close at 8,125.48. But it rose 8.49 points on the week.
Among the losers, food group Natfoods dropped 50 cents to 550, tobacco firm TSL and Alloys lost 25 cents each to 625 and 800 respectively while winery Afdis shed 10 cents to 415.

Electronics group Apex, tea and coffee producers EHPL, battery-maker Chloride, seed manufacturer and distributor Seedco and finance house UDC all eased five cents to 150, 130, 90, 235 and 250 respectively, while textiler David Whitehead slipped three cents to 80.

On the winning side, tobacco company Rothmans and agricultural investor Chemco leapt 300 cents each to 4,000 and 2,300 respectively, horticulture company Ariston rose 50 cents to 1,650, construction firm Mash at 220 and sugar producer Hippo at 950 each gained 20 cents.
Tyre manufacturer Dunlop at 160 and transport group Clan both put on 10 cents.

Minings were also fairly active and firmer with Falgold rising 25 cents to 125 while Wankie added five cents to 450. The seven-counter mining index gained 14.16 points to end at 1,214.45 -- a rise of 15.19 points on the week.
